author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: RevealX Enterprise and RevealX 360 send security detections from a detection notification rule with a Custom Webhook target, which can add a Bearer token, so they post straight to a Sophos NG-SIEM HTTP Ingest integration with no bridge. Choose Send for every detection update and a custom payload with the one-line copy of ExtraHop's suggested payload in README.md: HTTP Ingest reads each line of a body as a record, and ExtraHop's templates span many lines. Each security detection goes to the third-party alert schema: the detection type as the alert category, the risk score with ExtraHop's bands for severity (1 to 30 low, 31 to 79 medium, 80 to 99 high), src as the source, dst as the destination, and time (epoch milliseconds) as the event time. src is the participant that started the traffic, not always the offender, so both roles go to additional_data, with the detection URL, the most specific category, the first MITRE technique and the triage recommendation. A host name is the participant's hostname, or its device name when that is empty. Performance detections and the test notification stay generic. Samples are made up in the shape of ExtraHop's default webhook payload; one has the suggested custom payload's null host names, a JSON boolean for recommended and MITRE techniques as objects with an id and a name. Passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (95 of 95 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs). No built-in parser claimed these records in 5 Run Tests.
